## Step B — Keys: `testutil`, `keymap.Space`, `tea.KeyPressMsg`

**Files.** `internal/ui/testutil/testutil.go` (60 lines rewritten: `Key`, `Type`, `Paste`,
`IsText`, `Text`), its three test files (`keys_test.go`, `testutil_test.go`, `source_guard_test.go`),
`internal/ui/keymap/keymap.go` (`Space = "space"`), `internal/ui/keymap/legacy_key_scan_test.go`
(allow `KeyPressMsg`, `KeyReleaseMsg`, `PasteMsg`), a new guard in `internal/ui/keymap`, and the
115 production `tea.KeyMsg` sites in 49 files (sed `tea.KeyMsg` → `tea.KeyPressMsg`, then review the
38 gates).

**Interfaces (testutil).**
```go
func Key(name string) tea.KeyPressMsg   // {Code, Text, Mod}; String() is computed by v2, never imposed
func Keys(names ...string) []tea.Msg
func Type(s string) []tea.Msg           // one KeyPressMsg per rune; ' ' is Key("space")
func Paste(s string) tea.Msg            // tea.PasteMsg{Content: s}
func IsText(msg tea.Msg) bool           // KeyPressMsg with Text != "" and no ctrl/alt, or PasteMsg
func Text(msg tea.Msg) (string, bool)   // KeyPressMsg.Text, or PasteMsg.Content
```
Construction rules (from the spike): space `{Code: tea.KeySpace, Text: " "}`; rune `{Code: r, Text: string(r)}`;
`ctrl+x` `{Code: 'x', Mod: tea.ModCtrl}`; `alt+…` adds `ModAlt` **and clears `Text`** (otherwise
`String()` is `x`); `shift+tab` `{Code: tea.KeyTab, Mod: tea.ModShift}`; named keys `{Code: tea.KeyEnter}` etc.

**Tests (write first).**
| Test | Input → expected | Red |
|---|---|---|
| `TestKeyRoundTripsThroughString` (existing, kept) | every `namedKeys` name, `ctrl+a`…`ctrl+z`, `"y"`, `":"`, `"S"` → `Key(n).String() == n` | [R-compile] |
| `TestKeySpaceIsTheSpaceKey` (rewritten) | `Key(" ")` and `Key("space")` → `Code == tea.KeySpace`, `Text == " "`, `String() == "space"` | [R-compile] |
| `TestTheSpaceKeyIsNamedLikeKeymapSpace` (existing) | `Key("space").String() == keymap.Space` | [R-assert] once testutil is v2 and before `Space` flips: proves the flip is needed |
| `TestKeyAltPrefixSetsTheModifier` (rewritten) | `Key("alt+x").String() == "alt+x"`, `Text == ""` | [R-compile] |
| `TestPasteIsAPasteMsg` (replaces `TestPasteIsAPasteKeyMsg`) | `Paste("a\nb")` is `tea.PasteMsg{Content: "a\nb"}` | [R-compile] |
| `TestIsText` / `TestText` (rewritten) | rune, space, paste → true/text; `enter`, `ctrl+a`, `alt+x` → false | [R-compile] |
| `TestMsgsFlattensSequencesInOrder` (existing) | `tea.Sequence` still unpacks in order (bubbletea's `sequenceMsg` must stay `[]Cmd`) | [C] |
| `TestNoProductionCodeMatchesTheKeyMsgInterface` (new, `internal/ui/keymap`, AST, same scaffold as `legacy_key_scan_test.go`) + its detector self-test | a production `tea.KeyMsg` (type switch, assertion, parameter) → reported `path:line` | [R-assert] on today's code: 115 sites |
| `TestLegacyKeyReadsDetector` (existing, rows added) | `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg` → not flagged; `tea.KeyRunes`, `.Runes` → flagged | [R-assert]: `KeyPressMsg` starts with `Key`, flagged today |
| `TestGuardNoHandBuiltKeysOrColorProfile` (re-aimed) | a hand-built `tea.KeyPressMsg{…}` / `tea.PasteMsg{…}` in a `_test.go` outside testutil → reported | [R-compile] |

**Green checkpoint.** `go test ./internal/ui/testutil/ ./internal/ui/keymap/`.
Frontier: `go vet ./... 2>&1 | grep -cE 'KeyRunes|KeyType|KeyCtrl|\.Runes|\.Alt\b|tea\.KeyMsg'` → 0.

**Risks.** An uppercase action key (`S`, `N`…) is built `{Code: 'S', Text: "S"}`; a real legacy
terminal must deliver a key whose `String()` is `"S"` too. Covered by the manual check of one
uppercase action (G2). Release events reach `KeyMsg` only with keyboard enhancements, which are
not requested; the `KeyPressMsg` guard makes that moot.

## Step C — Router and option C (`Screen`, `Render`, `View() tea.View`), paste in the router
## Strategy: TDD when the intermediate commits do not compile

The `charm.land/*/v2` stack is coupled: `internal/app` imports every view, every view imports
`components`, which imports `textinput` and `theme`. **No commit between A1 and E builds the whole
module.** The commits are review units, not bisect points (spike §9). So:

1. **One branch, linear order A → G**, one commit per step (A and D split into sub-commits). Each
   commit changes one *category* across all files. Fixes found later for an earlier category go in
   the current commit and are noted in its body ("also: …"). Rewriting history to move them back
   is possible without an editor (`GIT_SEQUENCE_EDITOR=: git rebase -i --autosquash origin/main`
   with `fixup!` commits) but not required.
2. **Tests are written first in each step**, by the tester, from the "Tests" list of the step. A
   test is red for one of three reasons, stated per test:
   - **[R-assert]** it compiles and fails on today's code (e.g. theme validation, runewidth of a
     flag, the `KeyPressMsg` guard). Prove it red before the change.
   - **[R-compile]** it is written against the v2 API and does not compile until the step ends.
     The red proof is the compile error itself (`go vet ./<pkg>` output pasted in the progress file).
   - **[C]** characterization: green before and after (a guard that must not break). Prove it can
     fail by injecting the fault once (the detector self-tests already do this for the AST guards).
3. **Compile frontier.** Each step ends with a check that the frontier moved:
   - the packages listed under "Green checkpoint" build and their tests pass;
   - `go vet ./... 2>&1 | grep -cE '<pattern of the category just handled>'` is 0 (patterns per
     step below). The full error list goes to the scratchpad, never to the repo.
4. First `go build ./...` green: end of **E**. First `go test ./...` green: end of **F**.
   `mise run check` and `mise run test-race` green: end of **F**, again at the end of **G**.

## Step D3 — Paste reaches every focused field

**Why.** `tea.PasteMsg` is not a `tea.KeyPressMsg`. The router (C) forwards it to the active view
in edit mode, but 38 production gates switch on the key type only, so the view drops it silently.

**Files.** Each package with a text field or an edit mode: `components` (`FilterBar.Update` accepts
`tea.PasteMsg`, `WrappedInput`), `configuration`, `filebrowser`, `forge/auth`, `fuzzy`, `netdiag`
(3 files), `oci_resources` (4), `setup` (2), `status/components`, `templates`, `viewer` (search and
go-to-line prompts), `workspaces`, and the `FilterBar` users (`forge/explorer`, `security`,
`containers`, `jobsview`, `agentusageview`): wherever `Update` routes text to an input under
`case tea.KeyPressMsg`, add `case tea.PasteMsg` routed to the same field. Not a new abstraction:
the field's own `Update` already handles `PasteMsg`.

**Tests (write first).** One table-driven `paste_test.go` per package listed above, in the package
(they compile from the end of D1, except `internal/app`):
| Row | Steps → expected | Red |
|---|---|---|
| filter bar | `/` then `Paste("abc")` → `filterBar.SearchQuery() == "abc"`, rows filtered | [R-assert] once the package compiles: the view drops the `PasteMsg` |
| each form field | focus the field (↑/↓), `Paste("x y")` → field value `"x y"`; multi-line paste `"a\nb"` in a single-line field → `"a b"` | idem |
| no action | `Paste("D")` / `Paste("q")` in edit mode → no delete confirmation, no quit; outside edit mode the router drops it (C) | idem |
Existing: `TestTypedTextReachesTheFieldUnchanged` (`components`), `TestWrappedInputPaste`,
`component_form_test.go` paste rows ([C], must stay green).

**Green checkpoint.** `go test` on each package above (all except `dashboard` importers).
Frontier: `git grep -nE 'case tea\.KeyPressMsg' -- '*.go' ':!*_test.go'` reviewed: every file
that holds a `textinput.Model` or `WrappedInput` also has a `tea.PasteMsg` case (list in the
commit body).

**Risk.** A view that forwards the whole `msg` to its field already works; one that forwards only
the key does not. The per-package test is what tells them apart; reading the code is not enough.

## Step C — Router and option C (`Screen`, `Render`, `View() tea.View`), paste in the router

**Files.**
- 17 views: `Render() string` (the former `View() string`) plus a one-line `View() tea.View`:
  `about/view.go:75`, `agentusageview/view.go:21`, `configuration/view.go:28`, `containers/view.go:159`,
  `dashboard/view.go:20`, `filebrowser/view.go:22`, `forge/auth/view.go:107` (pointer receiver),
  `forge/explorer/view.go:22`, `jobsview/view.go:143`, `netdiag/view.go:18` (pointer receiver),
  `oci_resources/view.go:430`, `security/view.go:17`, `status/view.go:79`, `templates/view.go:128`,
  `viewer/view.go:17`, `workspaces/view.go:33`, and the setup wizard root `setup/fields.go:25`.
- `internal/app`: `app.go` (`views map[command.ViewType]Screen`, `App.Render`, `App.View`,
  `viewport.New` untouched until D1), the 35 `a.views[...] =` sites go through `setView` where the
  value is a `tea.Model`, `handlePasteMsg` (new, in the router's `update` switch).
- `main.go` (drop `tea.WithAltScreen()`), `internal/ui/setup/wizard.go` (idem; the wizard sets
  `AltScreen` in its own `View`).
- Tests: the 5 fake views and 2 program wrappers of `internal/app/*_test.go` (`programModel`,
  `timedProgramModel`), `router()`, `routerAt()`, `commanding()` take a `Screen`; `.View()` on a view
  model in tests → `.Render()`. **Let the compiler choose the sites** ("cannot use … (tea.View) as
  string"), instead of the spike's rename-all-then-revert-115: components keep `View() string` and
  never appear in the errors.
- Components (`datatable`, `components.*`, `status/components`, forms, `FilterBar`) keep `View() string`.
- No `handle*` signature changes (spike: 271 `handle*`, 429 `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)` returns, none touched).

**Interfaces.**
```go
// internal/app
type Screen interface {
	tea.Model
	Render() string
}
func (a *App) Render() string                              // the former View() string body
func (a *App) View() tea.View                              // v := tea.NewView(a.Render()); v.AltScreen = true; return v
func (a *App) setView(name command.ViewType, m tea.Model)  // asserts Screen, panics naming the view (H6)
func (a *App) handlePasteMsg(msg tea.PasteMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd)

Revue étape B (commit 0692c35) — verdict : OK, aucun point bloquant.

Vérifié

  • Conformité au plan B : testutil (Key/Keys/Type/Paste/IsText/Text), keymap.Space = "space", nouveau garde TestNoProductionCodeMatchesTheKeyMsgInterface + détecteur, legacy_key_scan_test réaligné, source_guard re-visé (KeyPressMsg/PasteMsg/KeyReleaseMsg interdits en littéral hors testutil). go test ./internal/ui/testutil ./internal/ui/keymap vert ; go vet ./... : 0 occurrence de KeyRunes|KeyType|KeyCtrl|.Runes|.Alt|tea.KeyMsg (frontière du plan atteinte). Les erreurs vet restantes (status/components/component_form.go, components/wrapped_input.go, creation_form.go) relèvent de D1.
  • Aucune comparaison " " en production ; les 8 gates de l'espace utilisent keymap.Space. Les tests passent de Key(" ") à Key("space") (équivalent, alias conservé).
  • Pas d'affaiblissement de test : les assertions Type/Runes/Alt sont réécrites en Code/Text/Mod avec le même sens, des lignes ajoutées (S, ":", alt+x pour IsText/Text, PasteMsg ne satisfait pas tea.KeyMsg). Le test v2 badV2 du source_guard est supprimé parce que le chemin d'import v1 n'existe plus (remplacé par des lignes KeyPressMsg/PasteMsg dans le cas bad).
  • Échantillon des gates (app.go, datatable, filter_bar, forge/auth, netdiag/forward_form, fuzzy, setup/confirm) : le changement de KeyMsg vers KeyPressMsg ne change pas le sens, sauf pour le collage (voir ci-dessous).
  • gofmt -w global : acceptable ; les 3 ou 4 fichiers hors périmètre ne sont que des réordonnancements d'imports (résultat de A1).

Important (à surveiller, non bloquant à ce stade)

  • Le collage ne passe plus par aucun gate : tea.PasteMsg n'est plus un KeyMsg, et aucune vue ne contient de case tea.PasteMsg (grep vide en production). Jusqu'à C (routeur) et D3 (38 gates), tout collage dans un champ est perdu silencieusement (ex. jeton dans forge/auth/update.go:28, qui retombe sur footer.Handle). Les tests paste_test.go, wrapped_input et component_form seront rouges de B à D3 : c'est prévu par le plan, mais D3 ne doit pas être sauté.

Mineur

  • internal/ui/forge/explorer/clone_indicator_test.go:3-5 : gofmt a placé tea "charm.land/..." avant "errors" dans le même bloc (groupe stdlib cassé). Un goimports/gci sur ce fichier suffit.

  • Les marqueurs [R-compile] / [R-assert] laissés dans les commentaires de tests (keys_test.go, théme) sont du bruit une fois l'étape terminée ; à retirer avant la fin de la story.
  • testutil.Key("S") donne {Code:'S', Text:"S", Mod:0} ; un vrai terminal peut envoyer Code 's' + ShiftedCode + ModShift (String() reste "S"). Sans impact tant que la production ne lit que String() ; couvert par le contrôle manuel G2 prévu.
  • Le garde legacy_key_scan ne contrôle pas les lectures de champs v2 (.Code, .Text, .Mod) en production ; la règle DEVDESK-200 « String() seulement » reste donc non vérifiée pour v2. À décider (garde ou règle écrite).

Rule 135 (Enter bascule la case dans OptionConfirmModal) : connu, pré-existant, non compté.

- Le `gofmt -w` global est acceptable : le bruit hors périmètre se limite à des réordonnancements d'imports issus de A1.

**Important (non bloquant à ce stade)**
- Le collage est perdu entre B et D3. `tea.PasteMsg` n'est plus un `KeyMsg` et aucune vue ne contient de `case tea.PasteMsg` en production. Un jeton collé dans `forge/auth/update.go:28` tombe donc sur `footer.Handle`. Les tests `paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input` et `component_form` seront rouges de B jusqu'à C (routeur) et D3, ce que le plan prévoit. D3 ne doit pas être sauté.

**Mineurs**
- `internal/ui/forge/explorer/clone_indicator_test.go:3-5` : gofmt a placé l'import `tea "charm.land/…"` avant `"errors"` dans le même bloc, ce qui casse le groupe stdlib. Un goimports sur ce fichier suffit.
- `internal/ui/theme/manager.go:229-230` : la phrase du commentaire de `validateTheme` est mal coupée.
- Les marqueurs `[R-compile]` / `[R-assert]` restent dans les commentaires de tests (`keys_test.go`, `theme_v2_test.go`). Ils sont à retirer avant la fin de la story.
- `testutil.Key("S")` produit `{Code:'S', Text:"S"}` sans modificateur. Un vrai terminal peut envoyer le code `s` avec `ModShift`, mais `String()` reste `"S"`. Sans impact tant que la production lit seulement `String()`. Le contrôle manuel G2 le couvre.
- Le garde `legacy_key_scan` ne vérifie pas les lectures de `.Code`, `.Text` et `.Mod` en production. La règle DEVDESK-200 « `String()` seulement » reste donc non vérifiée pour v2. À trancher : ajouter un garde ou écrire la règle.
